evals.prompt: Havli here - enamel cast-iron cookware, average order around $68. We want @noorcooksslow (92k on Instagram, slow-cooking recipes). Offer is 15% commission, 45-day cookie, paid on the 15th of the month after the sale clears. Her bio says "mgmt: talent@brightline-mgmt.co". I'd rather just DM her directly - going through an agent adds three weeks and I've had agents kill deals on me before. Heads up, our warehouse is mid-move so we can't ship samples for at least a month, and it's just me here so I don't have time to run intro calls. Write it.
evals.expected_output: A first-touch pitch addressed to the listed manager, with the commission mechanics front-loaded, a single CTA that the brand can actually honor, and a follow-up plan capped at three total messages.
expectations: Recommends pitching the listed manager or agent rather than sending a DM to the creator
States that the contact the creator publishes for business decides the channel, and that the ranking only breaks ties between published routes
Warns against opening a parallel direct thread to the creator while the manager thread is live
Does not present the DM as a lower-ranked but still available option once a manager is published
The drafted message states the 15% commission rate
The drafted message states the 45-day attribution window
The drafted message states the monthly payout timing
The drafted message includes an approximate per-sale earning derived from the $68 average order value (roughly $10)
The drafted message contains no rate card and no multi-deliverable campaign plan
The drafted message contains exactly one ask
Does not offer a product sample as the CTA, because no stock can ship
Does not offer a call as the CTA, because nobody is available to run one
The follow-up plan stops at three messages in total, counting the first touch

evals.prompt: I run partnerships at Rivenwork, a B2B compliance SaaS. I'm putting about 40 individual creator pitches into next quarter's plan and my VP won't sign off without a reply-rate target in the doc. What's the industry benchmark for creator outreach, and what number should I commit to? Also tell me what I should be tracking week to week so I can show progress.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to supply a published reply-rate benchmark, an explanation that none is trustworthy, and an own-log measurement plan with named columns and core KPIs.
expectations: Declines to supply an industry benchmark reply rate for creator outreach
States plainly that no trustworthy published reply-rate benchmark exists for creator outreach
Does not quote an "8.5% reply rate" figure
Does not quote a "99% ignored" claim about generic salutations
Does not quote a "90% response rate" practitioner claim
Does not present a "two personalized details raise replies by 56%" (5.6% vs 3.6%) figure as fact
Recommends building the team's own pitch log as the only valid benchmark
Names the log fields to capture: creator, channel, angle, sent date, follow-ups used, outcome, and days to reply
Says the log becomes a usable benchmark after roughly a dozen pitches
Lists reply rate, positive-reply rate, and days to first reply among the core KPIs
Includes which angles produced pitches that survived the downstream negotiation stage, recorded after that stage closes

evals.prompt: Mossline, DTC clean skincare. I'm pitching Ines Vardar (@inesvardar, 71k on Instagram, ingredient-breakdown videos) - offer is a $1,800 flat fee for one reel plus two stories. Walk me through the standard framework everyone uses for creator pitches, then write the email. Legal wants the FTC disclosure requirement and our 90-day category exclusivity spelled out in that first email so there are no surprises down the line.
evals.expected_output: A pitch that declines to invent a standard framework and keeps disclosure, exclusivity, and contract terms out of the cold message, routing the disclosure obligation elsewhere.
expectations: Does not present any framework as the industry standard for creator pitching
Does not invent a branded acronym or numbered "standard" method for creator outreach
States that no named industry-standard framework exists for creator pitching
Keeps FTC or disclosure language out of the first-touch message
Keeps the 90-day exclusivity demand out of the first-touch message
Keeps contract terms out of the first-touch message
Explains that disclosure, contract, and exclusivity topics belong after the creator agrees to talk, not in a cold pitch
Routes the substantive disclosure obligation to a separate disclosure-compliance skill rather than drafting label copy here
Does not claim the disclosure obligation is triggered by the contract or agreement date
The drafted message names the flat-fee model and the $1,800 figure without pasting a rate card
The drafted message uses no generic salutation such as "Dear influencer"
The drafted message is signed by a named human rather than a team alias

evals.prompt: Nullstack, observability SaaS. I want to sponsor Cold Start, the podcast Tobias Renn hosts for platform engineers - roughly 11k listeners an episode. Budget is confirmed at $4,000 for one mid-roll read plus a show-notes link, and he lists sponsors@coldstart.fm on the site. Our 2.0 launch is in 12 days and the slot has to be locked before then. Quick sanity check: is $4k right for 11k listeners? Then write the email and tell me how to chase it.
evals.expected_output: A deadline-adjusted pitch: near-zero-effort angle, reply-for-details CTA, single follow-up cadence, the flat fee named without a rate card, and no CPM figure presented as a market rate.
expectations: Re-ranks the default option order against the 12-day deadline and names which answer moved which option
Promotes a near-zero-effort personalization angle over the hour-of-grounding "specific content" angle because of the hard date
Recommends the reply-for-details CTA
Recommends a single follow-up at roughly five to seven business days instead of the two-follow-up default
Notes the cost of the single-follow-up cadence: a host who was simply travelling gets missed
The drafted message names the $4,000 flat fee
The drafted message contains no rate card and no attached campaign proposal
The deliverable stays a one-line sketch in the first message
The drafted message speaks to a business need the host's audience has, not only a product feature
Does not present podcast CPM ranges as market rates for an 11k-listener show
Declines to redesign or adjust the confirmed $4,000 offer, noting this work communicates the offer rather than setting it
The subject line names something specific to the show rather than a generic "sponsorship opportunity with Nullstack" pattern
The subject line contains no emoji

evals.prompt: Palta, small-batch hot sauce, we're four people. We want to send a 6-bottle box to @tinyfirekitchen (24k on TikTok, one-pan chili videos). No money in this at all - the box is the whole offer. Her bio says "DMs open, no email pls". We do have an application page at palta.co/creators I'd love her to fill out. Write the DM.
evals.expected_output: A 2-4 sentence DM with no links, stating plainly that the offer is product rather than payment, with one low-friction ask and no mass-funnel application link.
expectations: The drafted DM is two to four sentences long
The drafted DM contains no links
Does not paste the palta.co/creators application URL into the message
States plainly that the offer is product, not payment
Does not imply a fee, commission, or future payment
Does not offer exposure or audience growth as the compensation
Does not open on an asserted audience overlap as the angle
Opens on one verifiable creator-specific fact framed as audience fit rather than flattery
The drafted DM contains exactly one ask
Deletes the application-link CTA outright rather than ranking it last, because it routes an individually vetted creator into a mass funnel
Does not fabricate familiarity such as "I've been following you for ages"
Confirms the DM is the right channel here because the creator publishes no business email and no manager

evals.prompt: I emailed Rowan (@rowanbuildsdesks, 60k on YouTube, hand-tool woodworking) nine days ago about our chisel set - 10% commission, 30-day cookie, net-30 payout. Nothing back, not even an open as far as I can tell. Write me the follow-ups so I can queue them up, and tell me when to send each one.
evals.expected_output: One or two short follow-ups, each one or two sentences carrying a new angle, on the same channel, capped at three total messages, with an explicit close-the-file rule.
expectations: Each drafted follow-up is one or two sentences
No follow-up restates the commission rate, cookie window, or payout terms from the first touch
No follow-up restates the content of the first touch generally
Each follow-up carries one new small angle: a held-back proof point, an easier version of the ask, or a genuine timing hook
No follow-up uses "just checking in", "bumping this", or "did you see my email?"
No follow-up invents a deadline or manufactures scarcity
No follow-up uses guilt-tripping or chasing language
The sequence stops at three messages in total, counting the original email
The second follow-up lands roughly two weeks after the first follow-up
The follow-ups stay on the same channel as the first touch
Scores the follow-ups against the follow-up quality items only, not the full first-touch checklist
States that silence after the final message closes the file, reopened only with something genuinely new and never as a re-send
Runs a humanizer pass over the follow-up copy before presenting it

evals.prompt: Verdiga, contract analytics for legal ops teams. I pitched Amara Oyelaran's legal-ops newsletter at $2,500 flat for one dedicated issue. She just wrote back: "Interested, though $2,500 is low for a dedicated send - I'm usually at $4,000 - and I'd want to keep usage rights." Draft my reply countering at $3,000 with a six-month usage grant, and tell me what exclusivity window I should push for.
evals.expected_output: A hard stop at the positive reply: no counter drafted, remaining follow-ups cancelled, and a handoff package carrying the stated compensation facts unchanged into the negotiation stage.
expectations: Stops the outreach sequence at the positive reply
Does not draft the counter-offer or the negotiation reply
Hands off to a separate creator-negotiation skill rather than negotiating inside the pitch thread
Names that handoff target explicitly as the place where rates and deal terms are worked
Carries the $2,500 figure into the handoff unchanged
Does not invent, round, or adjust any of the stated compensation facts
Does not propose usage-rights terms
Does not propose an exclusivity window
Cancels the remaining planned follow-up touches
Produces handoff notes covering the compensation as stated, the deliverable mentioned, and the CTA promised
Logs the outcome and the days-to-reply against this pitch

evals.prompt: Ostara Labs, electrolyte tablets. Creator is @dunelanepace - 38k on Instagram, ultra-trail runner. Three weeks ago she posted a training-week recap and listed our tablets in her kit, unprompted, nobody paid her a cent. She also launched a paid training plan ten days ago, and honestly half our team uses her free race-pacing spreadsheet. She lists hello@dunelanepace.com. Offer is 18% commission, 30-day window, paid monthly. We've got pallets of product, a fulfilment partner who ships same day, and my calendar is wide open. Just write the email, you know the drill.
evals.expected_output: An angle brainstorm run before any drafting, landing on the she-already-uses-us angle, with the sample-on-reply CTA and its disclosure consequence flagged, delivered section by section.
expectations: Writes no pitch message until the user has explicitly picked an angle
Proposes two to three candidate angles with trade-offs and a recommendation
Recommends the angle that she already uses the brand, citing the unprompted kit-list mention
Ranks that angle above both the recent-launch angle and the specific-content angle
Does not offer an asserted audience overlap as a candidate angle
Asks brainstorming questions one at a time rather than in a single block
Recommends the sample-on-reply CTA over reply-for-details, because the product's value is obvious on contact and fulfilment ships without a second approval
Flags that a shipped sample creates a material connection the moment it lands, attaching a disclosure obligation to anything she posts about it whether or not a deal follows
Notes that a shipped sample cannot be un-shipped, unlike the other CTAs
Applies the swap test: substituting another creator's name would force a rewrite of the message
Presents the package section by section for validation rather than as one finished block
Delivers the artifact with labelled sections for the chosen angle, first touch, follow-up plan, stop rule, and handoff notes
